title.source: OXO：1990年，削皮器為什麼先改握柄？｜品牌故事
title.text: OXO: Why Change the Peeler Handle First in 1990? | Brand Stories

description.source:
一支削皮器從握不住，到真的交給另一雙手，握柄得改掉什麼？

跟著OXO的黏土與原型、被放棄的光滑泡狀方案、材料與連接設計，走到展前樣品、店內試削，以及具名作者記下的一次家庭使用。

起因與早期過程依品牌、具名設計者及館方回顧。專利是方案，館藏原型不是首款量產BOM；店家反應是當事人回憶，家庭試用是Lauralee Alben文章的個人記述，不推普遍療效。1997是文章刊出年，非已確定的試用年。匿名畫面為概念插圖。

description.text:
What must change in a peeler handle to take it from impossible to hold to something another pair of hands can try?

Follow OXO through clay, prototypes, a rejected smooth bubble design, materials and connections, then trade-show samples, a shop trial and one named author's account of family use.

The origins and early process follow retrospective accounts by the brand, named designers and museums. A patent describes proposals; a museum prototype is not the first production model's bill of materials. Shop reactions are recollections, and the family trial is Lauralee Alben's personal account, not evidence of general therapeutic benefits. 1997 is the publication year, not a confirmed trial date. Anonymous images are conceptual illustrations.

c10h02: MoMA收藏的OXO削皮器，只有十七點八公分長；
難題卻是，怎麼讓你的手握得住。
c10o08: 想像現在換你握，手指推著黏土，
原來細細的柄，外面多出可以調整的厚度。
c10o13: 要改現成廚具，先問會做菜的人，還是手不方便的人？
c10o14: 館方研究記下，團隊去問消費者、廚師，
也向紐約的關節炎群體了解困難。
c10v5o02: 介紹早期設計的訪談記下，團隊按手和手腕的動作，
替廚具分組。削皮器分到哪一組？
c10v5o03: 削皮器對應的動作，是推和拉。
你可以拿起它，試著把手帶向前，再帶回來。
c10v5o01: 館方另記下，不同版本的原型，也交給廚師、
一般使用者和紐約的關節炎群體試用。
c10r11: 斯托威爾說，把柄做成橢圓，
讓它較不容易轉動，也給了手中合適的方向感。
c10v5b01: 斯托威爾談過另一種早期方案：
光滑的握柄表面下，藏著可以變形的泡狀結構。
c10v5b03: 可是，那些初步設計最後被捨棄。
斯托威爾說，它們沒有讓人直覺看出能做什麼。
c10m01: 斯托威爾和同事麥可・卡拉漢，
在一九九〇年申請的握柄專利裡，畫出兩側凹下的區域。
c10m03: 結果，圖中的拇指和食指壓向兩側，
小片跟著變形，成為可以退讓的接觸區。
c10m09: 材料圖錄記下，這系列的握柄以射出成形製作，
材料因柔軟、暖觸感和耐用而被選用。
c10m11: 把材料想成還沒成形的顆粒，
再看最後可以被按下的小片，細節得一起做進外形。
c10m17: 品牌還提到，它適合與不鏽鋼等廚具材料結合，
也能應付洗碗機的使用環境。
c10a11: 作者另畫出上下粗細不同的柄芯，
交界形成一個階梯；內腔也做出相對的階梯。
c10a18a: 作者說，這樣的入口，讓手不太穩、
視力又不好的人，較容易把孔對到支撐鉤。
c10v5f02: 斯托威爾在後來的PBS訪談裡回憶，
離預定亮相的展會只剩兩個月，製造商還沒選定。
c10v5s04: 開場預告的黑柄試用，就在這裡：
削皮器用鏈條拴在胡蘿蔔碗上，讓進店的人伸手試。
c10v5u01: 設計作者艾爾本在一九九七年刊出的文章裡，
寫下親手用它的經驗。她先拿來做什麼？
c10l19: 我的答案是：要交給另一雙手，
握柄得先替人讓出能自己控制工具的位置。
c10l20: 也請你留言分享，想替家裡哪件小工具換個握柄，
以及最卡手的那個動作。

lines.source: 你連削皮器都握不住，晚餐還怎麼做？
lines.text: If you cannot even hold a peeler, how will you make dinner?

lines.source: MoMA收藏的OXO削皮器，只有十七點八公分長；難題卻是，怎麼讓你的手握得住。
lines.text: The OXO peeler in MoMA's collection is only 17.8 centimeters long. The hard part is making it something your hand can hold.

lines.source: 把時間往前挪，想像普羅旺斯的廚房，你正捏住細硬金屬柄。
lines.text: Go back in time and imagine a kitchen in Provence, with your fingers pinching a thin, rigid metal handle.

lines.source: 菜還沒削，手指就已經收得很勉強。
lines.text: You have not started peeling, yet your fingers are already struggling to close around it.

lines.source: 我想先看清楚，這雙手到底能放在哪。
lines.text: First, I want to see where those hands can actually fit.

lines.source: 桌上，一塊黏土等著被捏。
lines.text: On a table, a lump of clay waits to be shaped.

lines.source: 另一張桌，陌生的黑柄還等人伸手。
lines.text: On another table, an unfamiliar black handle waits for someone to reach out.

lines.source: 今天跟著OXO，追一支削皮器怎麼從握不住，走到交給別人試。
lines.text: Today, follow OXO and a peeler's journey from hard to hold to ready for someone else to try.

lines.source: 換了拿它的手，握柄究竟得改掉什麼？
lines.text: When a different hand picks it up, what exactly must change about the handle?

lines.source: 那雙難以收緊的手，來自貝琪・法伯。品牌回顧說，她有輕度關節炎。
lines.text: The hands that struggled to close belonged to Betsey Farber. The brand's retrospective says she had mild arthritis.

lines.source: 原本那種金屬削皮器，讓她做菜時很難拿。
lines.text: That kind of metal peeler was difficult for her to hold while cooking.

lines.source: 貝琪是建築師；丈夫山姆，則剛從自己創辦的廚具公司退休。
lines.text: Betsey was an architect. Her husband Sam had just retired from the kitchenware company he founded.

lines.source: 館方記下，夫妻在普羅旺斯享受做菜與藝術，麻煩就在這件小工具上。
lines.text: The museum notes that the couple enjoyed cooking and art in Provence, but this little tool caused trouble.

lines.source: 一塊能捏的材料，能不能先替她改掉握的地方？
lines.text: Could a moldable material first change the part she had to hold?

lines.source: 參與設計的戴文・斯托威爾後來回憶，貝琪把黏土捏在金屬削皮器外。
lines.text: Designer Davin Stowell later recalled that Betsey molded clay around the metal peeler.

lines.source: 她要找的，是拿起來更舒服的形狀。
lines.text: She was looking for a shape that felt more comfortable to hold.

lines.source: 想像現在換你握，手指推著黏土，原來細細的柄，外面多出可以調整的厚度。
lines.text: Imagine holding it yourself now. As your fingers push the clay, the thin handle gains an adjustable layer of thickness.

lines.source: 鬆開手，再看剛才哪裡被壓進去；你可以把不合手的一側，重新捏過。
lines.text: Let go and look at the indentations. You can reshape the side that does not fit your hand.

lines.source: 我想知道，原型先交到哪些人的手裡試？
lines.text: I want to know whose hands first tried the prototypes.

lines.source: 斯托威爾記得，山姆很堅持，這不能只是給少數人特別做的工具。
lines.text: Stowell recalled Sam insisting that this could not be a special tool made just for a small group.

lines.source: 他談的是生意上的現實：只做很小的市場，很難支撐這件產品。
lines.text: He was talking about a business reality: a tiny market would struggle to support the product.

lines.source: 山姆找上紐約Smart Design。要改現成廚具，先問會做菜的人，還是手不方便的人？
lines.text: Sam approached Smart Design in New York. To change existing kitchenware, do you first ask people who cook or people who struggle to use their hands?

lines.source: 館方研究記下，團隊去問消費者、廚師，也向紐約的關節炎群體了解困難。
lines.text: The museum's research says the team spoke to consumers and chefs, and asked arthritis groups in New York about their difficulties.

lines.source: 團隊的丹・福爾摩沙後來提過，專業廚師也可能有關節炎。
lines.text: Team member Dan Formosa later noted that professional chefs could have arthritis too.

lines.source: 他們還檢查現成廚具，看到生鏽金屬、裂開塑膠，以及不舒服的握柄。
lines.text: They also examined existing kitchen tools, finding rusted metal, cracked plastic and uncomfortable handles.

lines.source: 輪到你，把工具拿起來，再轉個方向；這個柄，跟得上你的動作嗎？
lines.text: Your turn: pick up the tool and change direction. Can this handle follow your movement?

lines.source: 介紹早期設計的訪談記下，團隊按手和手腕的動作，替廚具分組。削皮器分到哪一組？
lines.text: An interview about the early designs says the team grouped kitchen tools by hand and wrist movements. Where did the peeler belong?

lines.source: 削皮器對應的動作，是推和拉。你可以拿起它，試著把手帶向前，再帶回來。
lines.text: The peeler's movements were pushing and pulling. Pick it up and try moving your hand forward, then back.

lines.source: 後來的設計圖錄裡，木頭、橡膠、塑膠和泡棉，都成了握柄原型的材料。
lines.text: A later design catalogue shows wood, rubber, plastic and foam among the materials used for handle prototypes.

lines.source: 團隊做出數十個不同模型，放在桌上探索。
lines.text: The team made dozens of different models to explore on the table.

lines.source: 館方另記下，不同版本的原型，也交給廚師、一般使用者和紐約的關節炎群體試用。
lines.text: The museum also notes that different prototypes went to chefs, ordinary users and arthritis groups in New York for trials.

lines.source: 真正要交出去的那個柄，接下來得讓手指繞得回來。
lines.text: Next, the handle they would actually hand over had to let fingers wrap back around it.

lines.source: 館藏還保留一件木製握持研究，柄上做出四個凸起。
lines.text: The museum collection still holds a wooden grip study with four raised areas on its handle.

lines.source: 另一件泡棉、塑膠做的削皮器柄，仍帶著圓筒般的輪廓。
lines.text: Another peeler handle, made from foam and plastic, still has a cylindrical outline.

lines.source: 想像你從桌上拿起一個，沿掌心轉一點，再換下一個。
lines.text: Imagine picking one up from the table, turning it slightly in your palm, then trying the next.

lines.source: 斯托威爾說，太大抓不好，太細也抓不好。
lines.text: Stowell said that handles were hard to grip if they were too large or too thin.

lines.source: 大小之外，刀刃朝哪裡，也會跟著握的地方走。
lines.text: Beyond size, the blade's direction also depends on the part you hold.

lines.source: 想像你沿著蔬菜曲面轉一下手腕，刀還得留在你想去的方向。
lines.text: Imagine turning your wrist along a vegetable's curved surface. The blade must still point where you want it to go.

lines.source: 握柄如果在掌心裡轉掉，你還能把刀留在原來的角度嗎？
lines.text: If the handle spins in your palm, can you keep the blade at the same angle?

lines.source: 斯托威爾說，把柄做成橢圓，讓它較不容易轉動，也給了手中合適的方向感。
lines.text: Stowell said an oval handle was less likely to rotate and gave the hand a useful sense of direction.

lines.source: 我最在意你轉手腕的那一下。
lines.text: The moment you turn your wrist interests me most.

lines.source: 你可以想像，掌心沿較寬的一側包住，再讓手指從旁邊收回。
lines.text: Imagine wrapping your palm around the wider side, then bringing your fingers back around from the side.

lines.source: 手指碰到輪廓，表面要怎麼接住指腹？
lines.text: Once your fingers meet the outline, how should the surface receive their pads?

lines.source: 斯托威爾談過另一種早期方案：光滑的握柄表面下，藏著可以變形的泡狀結構。
lines.text: Stowell discussed another early idea: deformable bubbles hidden beneath a smooth handle surface.

lines.source: 他的想法是，手有時要捏緊再拉，有時只輕輕拉；握柄得能隨著握法變。
lines.text: His idea was that sometimes a hand grips tightly and pulls, and sometimes it pulls gently. The handle needed to adapt to the grip.

lines.source: 可是，那些初步設計最後被捨棄。斯托威爾說，它們沒有讓人直覺看出能做什麼。
lines.text: But those preliminary designs were abandoned. Stowell said they did not intuitively show people what they could do.

lines.source: 我會想，你第一次碰到這個光滑表面，要怎麼知道哪裡可以捏？
lines.text: I wonder how, on first touching that smooth surface, you would know where you could squeeze.

lines.source: 斯托威爾記得，和山姆討論時，附近正有一截腳踏車握把。
lines.text: Stowell remembered a piece of bicycle grip nearby as he talked with Sam.

lines.source: 它帶著細細的小鰭片，拇指和食指一捏，就會被壓得變形。
lines.text: It had thin little fins that deformed when pinched between thumb and forefinger.

lines.source: 換到你握這支小工具，那兩根手指，能不能也找到可以壓下去的位置？
lines.text: When you hold this little tool, could those two fingers also find a place that gives under pressure?

lines.source: 斯托威爾和同事麥可・卡拉漢，在一九九〇年申請的握柄專利裡，畫出兩側凹下的區域。
lines.text: In a handle patent filed in 1990, Stowell and his colleague Michael Callahan drew recessed areas on both sides.

lines.source: 凹處本身也做成橢圓，沿著柄伸展；文件說，要對到拇指和食指的指腹。
lines.text: The recesses are themselves oval and extend along the handle. The document says they align with the pads of the thumb and forefinger.

lines.source: 每一側都安排一排小鰭片，片與片之間，留著間隔。
lines.text: Each side has a row of little fins, with spaces between them.

lines.source: 結果，圖中的拇指和食指壓向兩側，小片跟著變形，成為可以退讓的接觸區。
lines.text: In the drawing, the thumb and forefinger press against the sides, deforming the fins into a yielding contact area.

lines.source: 我想直接捏一次，試試這個位置。
lines.text: I want to squeeze that spot myself and try it.

lines.source: 這些細節得真的能彎，究竟要選什麼材料？
lines.text: For these details to actually bend, what material should they choose?

lines.source: 館藏資料把早期削皮器的柄記為Santoprene，一種熱塑性橡膠。
lines.text: Museum records identify the early peeler's handle as Santoprene, a thermoplastic rubber.

lines.source: 材料圖錄記下，這系列的握柄以射出成形製作，材料因柔軟、暖觸感和耐用而被選用。
lines.text: A materials catalogue says this range's handles were injection-molded, with the material selected for softness, a warm feel and durability.

lines.source: 沒想到，品牌回顧的選材線索，還伸進工業裡，像設備內部的密封墊。
lines.text: Surprisingly, the brand's retrospective traces the material search into industrial uses, such as seals inside equipment.

lines.source: 把材料想成還沒成形的顆粒，再看最後可以被按下的小片，細節得一起做進外形。
lines.text: Imagine the material as pellets before molding, then look at the little fins you can press down. Those details must be formed as part of the shape.

lines.source: 偏偏，你真正下廚的時候，手上還可能有水。
lines.text: Yet when you actually cook, your hands may also be wet.

lines.source: 品牌回顧說，選這種熱塑性橡膠，也看上了濕的時候仍不易滑的特性。
lines.text: The brand's retrospective says they also chose this thermoplastic rubber for its resistance to slipping when wet.

lines.source: 想像你剛洗過菜，拿回那支刀。
lines.text: Imagine picking the peeler up again just after washing vegetables.

lines.source: 品牌還提到，它適合與不鏽鋼等廚具材料結合，也能應付洗碗機的使用環境。
lines.text: The brand also says it combines well with kitchenware materials such as stainless steel and can withstand dishwasher use.

lines.source: 你削完菜，把工具洗乾淨，再讓它回到抽屜。
lines.text: You finish peeling, wash the tool and return it to the drawer.

lines.source: 但是，你握著軟柄，刀刃的方向要怎麼接過去？
lines.text: But when you hold a soft handle, how does it carry the blade's direction through?

lines.source: 那份握柄專利，把一個腔室畫在裡面，沿著柄的長方向伸進去。
lines.text: That handle patent draws an internal cavity extending lengthwise into the handle.

lines.source: 工具的柄芯插進腔室，尺寸配合，讓外面的握柄套住它。
lines.text: The tool's shank enters the cavity, its dimensions fitting so the outer handle surrounds it.

lines.source: 你可以想像，一隻手扶著空心軟柄，另一隻手把硬的連接部位推入。
lines.text: Imagine one hand holding the hollow, soft handle while the other pushes the rigid connecting part inside.

lines.source: 沒想到，文件先用一支刷子來畫結構，也把削皮器列進可以套用的工具。
lines.text: Unexpectedly, the document first uses a brush to illustrate the structure, while also listing peelers among the tools it can apply to.

lines.source: 我會擔心你往回拉的那一下：手裡會不會只剩軟柄，工具卻沒跟過來？
lines.text: I worry about the moment you pull back. Could only the soft handle remain in your hand, with the tool left behind?

lines.source: 文件的一個方案，讓柄芯擴大的頭部貼住柄端，再用黏結劑固定。
lines.text: One proposal in the document places the shank's enlarged head against the handle's end, then secures it with adhesive.

lines.source: 如果連接不靠這一道黏結，柄芯的形狀還能再做什麼？
lines.text: If the connection does not rely on that adhesive, what else could the shank's shape do?

lines.source: 作者另畫出上下粗細不同的柄芯，交界形成一個階梯；內腔也做出相對的階梯。
lines.text: The authors also draw a shank with different thicknesses above and below, forming a step. The cavity has a matching step.

lines.source: 兩處對上，便用這個結構抵抗握柄被抽走。
lines.text: When those two parts align, the structure resists the handle being pulled off.

lines.source: 柄尾那個大孔，除了掛起來，還能把手放到哪？
lines.text: Besides hanging it up, where else could your fingers go in that large hole at the end?

lines.source: 專利描述，拇指與食指伸進兩側孔口，捏住柄尾，必要時便能拉動工具。
lines.text: The patent describes inserting the thumb and forefinger into the openings on either side, pinching the handle's end to pull the tool when needed.

lines.source: 掛回去那一下，孔口的形狀還能幫忙嗎？
lines.text: When you hang it back up, could the shape of the opening help too?

lines.source: 文件把孔口做成兩邊較寬、往中間縮的形狀。
lines.text: The document shapes the opening wider at both sides and narrower toward the middle.

lines.source: 作者說，這樣的入口，讓手不太穩、視力又不好的人，較容易把孔對到支撐鉤。
lines.text: The authors say this entrance makes it easier for people with unsteady hands and poor vision to align the hole with a support hook.

lines.source: 你可以想像，手正把柄送向鉤子，開口先迎過去，再讓鉤穿進去。
lines.text: Imagine bringing the handle toward the hook, letting the opening meet it first, then letting the hook pass through.

lines.source: 另一件館藏削皮器原型，把問題帶到刀片：它靠哪裡接住？
lines.text: Another museum peeler prototype brings the question to the blade: what holds it in place?

lines.source: 刀片是能轉動的金屬片，支架的上端和下端，各有一個孔。
lines.text: The blade is a pivoting metal strip, with one hole at the top and another at the bottom of its support.

lines.source: 它靠兩個接點，分別落在這兩個孔裡。
lines.text: Two attachment points sit in those two holes.

lines.source: 要把這件工具交出去，能找到願意做的工廠嗎？
lines.text: To get this tool into other hands, could they find a factory willing to make it?

lines.source: 斯托威爾在後來的PBS訪談裡回憶，離預定亮相的展會只剩兩個月，製造商還沒選定。
lines.text: In a later PBS interview, Stowell recalled that with only two months until the planned trade-show debut, a manufacturer had still not been chosen.

lines.source: 山姆想起以前做廚具時，合作過的一家日本製造商。
lines.text: Sam remembered a Japanese manufacturer he had worked with in his earlier kitchenware business.

lines.source: 他們去了工廠，得到的答覆是：願意製作。
lines.text: They visited the factory and received the answer: yes, they would make it.

lines.source: 我聽到這裡，會先盯著展會開門的時間。換你等樣品，還能等到哪一天？
lines.text: Hearing that, I start watching the trade show's opening date. If you were waiting for samples, how late could you wait?

lines.source: 展會開門前兩天，一個箱子到了。
lines.text: Two days before the show opened, a box arrived.

lines.source: 他說，箱裡裝著樣品；他用「完美」形容它們。
lines.text: He said it contained samples, which he described as perfect.

lines.source: 他記得，展會是在一九九〇年五月開門的。
lines.text: He remembered the show opening in May 1990.

lines.source: 如果你是店家，把這些工具買回去，客人會直接伸手嗎？
lines.text: If you stocked these tools in your shop, would customers simply reach for them?

lines.source: 斯托威爾點名，家用品店萊克特斯買下整條產品線。
lines.text: Stowell named the housewares retailer Lechters as buying the whole product line.

lines.source: 可是他記得，貨賣得沒有店家期待的快。
lines.text: But he recalled that sales were slower than the retailer had expected.

lines.source: 山姆的主意，是先擺出一碗胡蘿蔔。
lines.text: Sam's idea was to put out a bowl of carrots first.

lines.source: 開場預告的黑柄試用，就在這裡：削皮器用鏈條拴在胡蘿蔔碗上，讓進店的人伸手試。
lines.text: Here is the black-handle trial teased at the start: a peeler chained to a bowl of carrots, inviting shoppers to try it.

lines.source: 想像你走到桌邊，把刀拿起來，手指先落在柄上，再讓刀片碰到食材。
lines.text: Imagine walking to the table and picking it up, your fingers settling on the handle before the blade touches the food.

lines.source: 手跟著往前帶，刀片開始工作。
lines.text: Your hand moves forward and the blade starts working.

lines.source: 沒想到，照他的回憶，開放試削後，貨就賣得很快。
lines.text: Unexpectedly, in his recollection, sales picked up quickly after customers could try peeling.

lines.source: 後來介紹這套設計的文章，還記下包裝讓握柄露在外面的做法。
lines.text: A later article about the design also noted packaging that left the handle exposed.

lines.source: 顧客買之前，就能伸手摸一摸，再捏一捏。
lines.text: Before buying, customers could reach out, touch it and give it a squeeze.

lines.source: 設計作者艾爾本在一九九七年刊出的文章裡，寫下親手用它的經驗。她先拿來做什麼？
lines.text: In an article published in 1997, design writer Alben described using it herself. What did she try first?

lines.source: 她買了一支，拿來削胡蘿蔔。她說，自己用得很愉快。
lines.text: She bought one and peeled carrots with it. She said she enjoyed using it.

lines.source: 她又把削皮器帶到丈夫父母那裡，讓吉姆和寶拉試。
lines.text: She then took the peeler to her husband's parents, Jim and Paula, for them to try.

lines.source: 她記下他們一開始的反應：很舒服，大黑柄容易握，不用捏得那麼用力。
lines.text: She recorded their first reactions: comfortable, a big black handle that was easy to hold, and less need to squeeze hard.

lines.source: 如果換你，會只把它握著，還是真的拿一顆馬鈴薯來？
lines.text: What about you? Would you just hold it, or actually fetch a potato?

lines.source: 艾爾本寫道，他們輪流拿削皮器削馬鈴薯。
lines.text: Alben wrote that they took turns peeling potatoes with it.

lines.source: 她記下他們還說，刀很利，朝自己或往外削，都能用。
lines.text: She also recorded them saying that the blade was sharp and worked when peeling toward themselves or away.

lines.source: 我讀到這裡，反而等著看，他們會怎麼把它收起來。
lines.text: Reading this, I find myself waiting to see how they will put it away.

lines.source: 文章裡，他們又說：試試把它掛起來吧。
lines.text: In the article, they then said: let's try hanging it up.

lines.source: 接著的回答是：行，這樣也可以。
lines.text: The next response was: yes, that works too.

lines.source: 然後，兩人拿出原本那支金屬削皮器。
lines.text: Then the two of them brought out their original metal peeler.

lines.source: 他們把新舊兩支，並排拿著。
lines.text: They held the new and old peelers side by side.

lines.source: 最後，把舊的那支丟進垃圾桶。
lines.text: Finally, they threw the old one into the trash.

lines.source: 我的答案是：要交給另一雙手，握柄得先替人讓出能自己控制工具的位置。
lines.text: My answer is this: to pass a tool to another pair of hands, its handle must first make room for people to control it themselves.

lines.source: 也請你留言分享，想替家裡哪件小工具換個握柄，以及最卡手的那個動作。
lines.text: Tell me in the comments which small tool at home you would give a new handle, and which movement is hardest on your hand.

lines.source: 想繼續看設計怎麼改變你每天做的事，歡迎訂閱這個頻道。
lines.text: Subscribe to the channel to keep exploring how design changes the things you do every day.
